assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello unified electronic-structure DFT with molecular dynamics in 1985, making finite-temperature, ab initio simulation of real materials, liquids and bonding changes routine. Original, conceptually clear and of enormous lasting impact across condensed matter, chemistry and materials science; it underpins the computational materials toolchain I work in.
assessment.attribution: Car and Parrinello are the two authors of the decisive 1985 paper, so a two-person prize is clean. Later code developments by many others are not needed for the core credit.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and independent reimplementation in many codes; the reproducibility of DFT results across codes is well established. Recognition is, if anything, overdue, and computation-as-discovery is the main committee question.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards a method as a physical discovery of the kind Nobel physics usually requires, given overlap with the 1998 chemistry prize for DFT.
I have not independently verified citation counts or priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter. A genuine new quantum behaviour in a material, and a case where theory and experiment fit together quantitatively.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery. The first-author experimental contributor (Yuan Cao) is not in the credited names, and Cory Dean's group and others are also relevant, so credit is tight but workable with these three.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated and superconducting phases and extended to related moire systems. Open questions on the pairing mechanism remain, but the discovery itself is robust and the field is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: Unresolved pairing mechanism and sample-to-sample variability.
Supplied credit omits the experimental lead student and other moire pioneers; attribution is not unique.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and the HgTe experimental observation of helical edge transport, established a new topological classification of electronic states with wide influence on condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theory; Molenkamp led the experimental confirmation in HgTe wells. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe route and Konig et al. observed it, and three-dimensional topological insulators involved other groups, so the three-person split omits some contributors.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by transport and ARPES in multiple materials for roughly two decades. Overlaps with the 2016 topological-phase prize but is distinct in time-reversal symmetry and materials realization.
uncertainties: Priority claims around HgTe theory (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) versus Kane-Mele.
Possible concern that this is close to the 2016 prize scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's 2003 magic-wavelength lattice proposal and the subsequent realization of optical lattice clocks gave stability at the 10^-18 level, with consequences for metrology, redefinition of the second, geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. Clear, original and exceptionally precise.
assessment.attribution: Katori invented the concept and Ye led the leading implementations and record accuracy. A two-person prize is natural, though the 2005 prize already honoured Hall and Hansch for the comb.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs confirm the performance, and international timekeeping is moving toward optical redefinition, making the timing good.
uncertainties: Other pioneers in neutral-atom and ion optical clocks may be argued for.
Not a condensed-matter topic, so I defer partly to colleagues in atomic physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realizing the Mott insulator transition in optical lattices and subsequent quantum simulation of Hubbard-type models gives a controlled platform for strongly correlated matter, linking directly to questions in my own field with a clean theoretical mapping.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-Mott transition (2002); Esslinger realized fermionic Hubbard physics; Zoller and Jaksch provided the key proposal. Choosing three leaves Zoller out, so credit is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed and still productive; quantum-gas microscopes and fermionic Hubbard simulations are mature, though the 2001 and 2012 prizes partly overlap with this area.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for ultracold gases and manipulation of quantum systems.
Allocation among theory proposal and several experimental groups is contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hosono's 2008 discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx started a second family of high-Tc superconductors, with rapid rise of Tc beyond 50 K and a rich interplay of magnetism, nematicity and superconductivity relevant to my own interests in magnetic materials.
assessment.attribution: Hosono made the initial discovery; Chen and Zhao's groups quickly raised Tc in the Sm-based compounds. Credit for the subsequent rise is sound, but Hosono is the clear core.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and extensively over 15 years, but the microscopic pairing mechanism remains unsettled and no practical application has emerged, which weakens the case compared to cuprates.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to recognize a second class of high-Tc without a theoretical explanation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the spin Hall effect by Dyakonov and Perel and its optical and electrical observation in semiconductors created a core mechanism of spintronics, relevant for spin-orbit torque devices in magnetic memory.
assessment.attribution: Dyakonov is the originator of the prediction; Awschalom's group made the 2004 optical observation, and Jungwirth's group the electrical and theoretical development. Others such as Hirsch, Zhang, Kato and Wunderlich are also tied to this story, and Perel is deceased, so credit is spread.
assessment.maturity: The effect is well confirmed and has led to applications such as spin-orbit-torque switching, so maturity is high, but the exact split of credit is disputed.
uncertainties: Strongly contested attribution; the supplied three-name list may not capture the best configuration.
Intrinsic versus extrinsic mechanisms involve additional contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of superconductivity in the Bechgaard salts in 1980 was the first organic superconductor, opening a field of low-dimensional correlated conductors, spin-density waves and unconventional pairing. It is an example of a new quantum behaviour in an unexpected class of materials.
assessment.attribution: Jérome and Bechgaard are the decisive pair for the 1980 discovery; Saito's contributions are later (BEDT-TTF family), so a two-person prize of Jérome and Bechgaard would be the cleaner configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed for over 40 years, though the impact has been more conceptual than technological, and recognition is long delayed.
uncertainties: Impact on broader physics may be judged narrower than the other candidates.
Saito's inclusion is optional and debatable.
